#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run every local check on examples/. Nothing here contacts AWS, GitHub settings or any
# other live system. Tools that are not installed are SKIPPED with a message, never
# reported as passed. Set ACTIONLINT / ZIZMOR to the binaries if they are not on PATH.
set -uo pipefail
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1

ACTIONLINT="${ACTIONLINT:-actionlint}"
ZIZMOR="${ZIZMOR:-zizmor}"
fail=0
skipped=()

section() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$1"; }
have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
run() { "$@" || { echo "FAILED: $*"; fail=1; }; }

section "tool versions"
python3 --version
python3 -c 'from importlib.metadata import version as v; print("jsonschema", v("jsonschema"), "| PyYAML", v("PyYAML"))'
for t in jq yamllint shellcheck "$ACTIONLINT" "$ZIZMOR"; do
  if have "$t"; then printf '%s: %s\n' "$(basename "$t")" "$("$t" --version 2>&1 | head -1)"
  else printf '%s: not installed\n' "$(basename "$t")"; fi
done

section "JSON syntax (jq)"
if have jq; then
  while IFS= read -r f; do run jq empty "$f"; done < <(find . -name '*.json' -not -path './*/node_modules/*' | sort)
  echo "checked $(find . -name '*.json' -not -path './*/node_modules/*' | wc -l) files"
else skipped+=("jq"); echo "SKIPPED: jq not installed"; fi

section "YAML style (yamllint)"
if have yamllint; then
  run yamllint -d '{extends: default, rules: {line-length: {max: 120}, document-start: disable, truthy: {check-keys: false}, comments: {min-spaces-from-content: 1}}}' github/workflows
else skipped+=("yamllint"); echo "SKIPPED: yamllint not installed"; fi

section "GitHub Actions (actionlint)"
if have "$ACTIONLINT"; then
  # actionlint 1.7.12 (latest, March 2026) predates GitHub's same-repository `$/` syntax for
  # reusable workflows (GitHub docs, workflow-syntax, jobs.<job_id>.uses). Only that message
  # is ignored.
  SC=(); have shellcheck && SC=(-shellcheck "$(command -v shellcheck)")
  run "$ACTIONLINT" "${SC[@]}" -ignore 'reusable workflow call "\$/' github/workflows/*.yml
  echo "actionlint done"
else skipped+=("actionlint"); echo "SKIPPED: actionlint not installed"; fi

section "GitHub Actions security (zizmor, offline, auditor persona)"
if have "$ZIZMOR"; then
  run "$ZIZMOR" --offline --no-progress --persona=auditor github/workflows/*.yml
else skipped+=("zizmor"); echo "SKIPPED: zizmor not installed"; fi

section "unit tests (python3 -m unittest)"
run python3 -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -v

section "result"
if [ ${#skipped[@]} -gt 0 ]; then echo "SKIPPED (not verified): ${skipped[*]}"; fi
if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then echo "RESULT: FAILED"; exit 1; fi
echo "RESULT: all executed checks passed"

content.content:
* `$/.github/workflows/{filename}` for a reusable workflow in the same repository. This is the recommended syntax for referencing a reusable workflow in the same repository. This syntax is not available in {% data variables.product.prodname_ghe_server %}.
* `{owner}/{repo}/.github/workflows/{filename}@{ref}` for reusable workflows in {% ifversion fpt %}public and private{% elsif ghec or ghes %}public, internal and private{% endif %} repositories.
* `./.github/workflows/{filename}` for reusable workflows in the same repository.

When you reference a reusable workflow with `{owner}/{repo}` and `@{ref}`, the `{ref}` can be a SHA, a release tag, or a branch name. If a release tag and a branch have the same name, the release tag takes precedence over the branch name. Using the commit SHA is the safest option for stability and security. For more information, see [AUTOTITLE](/actions/reference/security/secure-use#reusing-third-party-workflows).

When you reference a reusable workflow in the same repository using `$/` or `./` (without `{owner}/{repo}` and `@{ref}`), the called workflow is from the same commit as the caller workflow. A `$/` reference must not include an `@{ref}` suffix, and `$/` is not available in {% data variables.product.prodname_ghe_server %}. Ref prefixes such as `refs/heads` and `refs/tags` are not allowed. You cannot use contexts or expressions in this keyword.
----
{% ifversion actions-nga %}

This means that there can be at most one running job or workflow in a concurrency group at any time. When a concurrent job or workflow is queued, if another job or workflow using the same concurrency group in the repository is in progress, the queued job or workflow will be `pending`. By default, any existing `pending` job or workflow in the same concurrency group will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place.

{% else %}

This means that there can be at most one running and one pending job in a concurrency group at any time. When a concurrent job or workflow is queued, if another job or workflow using the same concurrency group in the repository is in progress, the queued job or workflow will be `pending`. Any existing `pending` job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place.

{% endif %}

To also cancel any currently running job or workflow in the same concurrency group, specify `cancel-in-progress: true`. To conditionally cancel currently running jobs or workflows in the same concurrency group, you can specify `cancel-in-progress` as an expression with any of the allowed expression contexts.

{% ifversion actions-nga %}

To allow more than one `pending` job or workflow run to wait in the same concurrency group, use the optional `queue` property. The `queue` property accepts the following values:

* `single` (default): At most one job or workflow run can be `pending` in the concurrency group. When a new job or workflow run is queued, any existing `pending` job or workflow run in the same group is canceled and replaced.
* `max`: Up to 100 jobs or workflow runs can be `pending` in the concurrency group. When the queue is full, any additional jobs or workflow runs are canceled.

The combination of `queue: max` and `cancel-in-progress: true` is not allowed and will result in a workflow validation error.

{% endif %}

> [!NOTE]
> * The concurrency group name is case insensitive. For example, `prod` and `Prod` will be treated as the same concurrency group.
> * Jobs or workflow runs in the same concurrency group are processed in first-in-first-out (FIFO) order according to the time each one started waiting on the concurrency group, not the time each workflow was dispatched. Since the actual start time of a job or run may vary, ordering is not guaranteed.

### Example: Using concurrency and the default behavior

The default behavior of {% data variables.product.prodname_actions %} is to allow multiple jobs or workflow runs to run concurrently. The `concurrency` keyword allows you to control the concurrency of workflow runs.

## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level

**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and
no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an
unavailable primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how
many. Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level; that adds a
second approval by an owner of the same stack, which keeps it to two people (OD8). Confirmed by the owner
(OD13): the original author opens the approval PR and the first approver
approves it. If the first approver is unavailable, another owner of the stack approves; that makes
three people and is recorded as a deviation, counted monthly (OD11). A cross-team PR needs one
approval, as GitHub accepts one on-call group member for files of several owner teams (OD10,
OD9, 📖 R3.2.7); domain review there is a recommendation, counted in the monthly report. A real-data read is not a change and has its own rule, L3-data. Incidents use the same
path with faster people, not fewer security checks.

| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue and the rest of the canonical list in layer 5; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher. L3 paths (workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, the SCP stack): the L3 owner team only (OD13); IAM-only stacks are deployable, so the L3 owner team plus the on-call group (OD9). L3 content inside a domain file (an IAM statement in `serverless.yml`, a stateful delete): the stack's owner, then the risk stop (OD8). In incidents: the on-call approver for deployable paths (OD9); paths that define the process (CODEOWNERS, agent config, catalogue, workflows) wait for the L3 owner team | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b); incidents only, as the owner accepted it (Options §9 Q2); the on-call approver counts as owner of the service in the request (OD13) | layer 7 |
| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9; at night, see layer 6 | layer 6 |

`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
the whole team (OD3). With code-owner review on, every PR, L2 included, needs an approval from an
owner of the files it touches (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7; per-file behaviour ⚠️ not a separate research row).
What differs at L3 is **which team** owns the path: L3 paths are owned in CODEOWNERS by a designated
L3 owner team (deployable L3 paths also by the on-call group, OD9), L2 paths by their domain team; and IaC changes at L3 meet the
risk stop. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files, so they are approved by
the stack's owners, not the L3 team (OD8); automated checks make up for this: IAM Access Analyzer
`check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and the Pulumi policy pack (📖 R4.2.2), both from phase 2 (layer 5). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need the L3 owner team, not
the domain team that edits it most.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
- **L3 approvals [design]:** CODEOWNERS plus code-owner review only, no path-based required
  reviewers rule. That rule (📖 R3.2.4) asks for approvals from specific teams, which the on-call
  group would not satisfy at night, and how it combines several teams is not researched (⚠️), so it
  would break OD9 or add a third person. GitHub stops the author from approving (📖 R3.3.1). A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5), set by a dedicated GitHub App that reacts to review events and is the pinned source [design; hosting, key storage and whether its key counts against S2 are not researched, ⚠️ G19], adds what
  the rules cannot: for app-opened PRs it excludes the person who triggered the agent, and it counts
  only human approvals, since an app's approval might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3). A workflow
  instead of an app is weaker: pinning the source to GitHub Actions likely lets any workflow set a
  check of the same name, and the trigger that runs on review events from trusted code is not
  researched (⚠️ G19).
- **Who approves at night (OD9):** a fixed GitHub team with write permission (owners without it
  are silently not assigned, 📖 R3.2.7; the CODEOWNERS validation check covers this), the on-call approvers, is listed as
  co-owner on every deployable path in CODEOWNERS (infrastructure and service code), next to the
  domain team. Confirmed by the owner (OD13): the group does **not** co-own the paths that
  define the process (`.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md` and agent config, catalogue); those stay
  with the L3 owner team only. If a broken workflow blocks a night fix, the pipeline counts as
  unavailable and the JIT fallback applies (layer 7). One primary and one backup from that team are on call. Technically any member can approve any
  path; by rule the primary approves and the backup only if the primary is unavailable (OD2).
  Membership is fixed, not changed per shift [design]. GitHub team membership is set in organization
  settings, not by a PR; managing it as code (e.g. with Pulumi's GitHub provider) and the audit
  event for a membership change are not researched (⚠️ G16). Meanwhile the layer-7 settings
  comparison includes the group's member list. Cost: an approval from any
  listed owner satisfies code-owner review (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days a member could approve
  another domain's PR, on or off shift. Mitigation [design]: process rule "approve another
  domain's PR only if it carries the `incident` label and you are on shift", and a monthly report of
  every cross-domain approval by group members on PRs without that label (layer 7). Whether Papaya's team size allows full coverage is unknown
  (§1, S7).
- **Risk stop [design]:** applies to every deploy, whatever the level. The deploy job previews prod;
  on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change, a network or security-group change, or an advisory
  policy finding (from phase 2) it stops and posts the filtered preview. The original author opens a second PR that adds
  `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` (`<sha>` = the stopped commit) holding that SHA and the
  preview hash; the workflow does not open it, because the setting that lets Actions create and approve PRs stays
  off (📖 R3.3.3; ⚠️ R3.6 #3). CODEOWNERS on `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` names the owners of that stack and the
  on-call group (OD8, OD9). The approver is ≠ author and may be the first PR's approver, who now sees
  the prod diff. Merging it triggers the deploy on the new HEAD, which previews again and continues
  only if the hash matches the approved one; if another PR merged in between, the hash differs and
  the deploy stops again (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). Cost: while a stack is
  stopped, later merges to that stack stop too until a matching approval lands; in an incident, a
  risky change already waiting on `main` blocks the fix for the same stack until it is approved or
  reverted. A
  `mandatory` policy violation always blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2): the fix is a code change, or a
  change to the policy pack through its own L3 PR. Preview output is filtered for
  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4).
- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
- **State:** writable by deploy roles (and possibly the drift role, layer 7); Pulumi
  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1). The risk
  stop is described for Pulumi and Serverless only; for k0s manifests (RBAC changes are the IAM
  equivalent) a `kubectl diff`-based stop is a candidate, not researched (⚠️ G1). Firebase deploys
  have no preview step in this design (⚠️ G2).
- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
  slow unrelated tests skipped [design]. A required check skipped by a path filter may stay
  pending and block the merge (open, Options §8); this directly affects S7.

**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)

The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
unavailable).

1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
3. R, a co-owner of `serverless.yml` through the on-call group (OD9), reviews the diff. If R
   catches a missing queue change, R does not fix it (OD7): E pushes the fix, the stale approval is
   dismissed, and R approves again, one more review round (Options §6). E merges.
4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.

**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks); run log and preview artifact, exported because
retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.

**Cost / value.** One approver for every prod change, from the owners of the path; two approvals,
usually by the same approver, when the risk stop fires (OD13; OD11). Cross-team PRs: one approval (OD10). None in non-prod.
Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

157:- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod role trusts only the `production`
## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening

**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
checks as human code (S10).

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
  deploys may need a stored credential in GitHub: a kubeconfig or token for k0s, a Firebase token or
  service-account key for Firebase Hosting. The owner accepts this as an exception to S2 = 0 until it
  is checked whether k0s and Firebase deploys can use OIDC (OD1, OD6). Conditions [design]:
  - stored only as an **environment secret of `production`**, never as a repository secret. Anyone
    with write access can read repository secrets (📖 R3.5.3b), which would turn the exception into
    standing prod write for every engineer and their agent. Environment secrets and a deployment
    branch rule limited to `main` are available on Team for private repos (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3), and
    only the reviewed deploy workflow references the environment (layer 3);
  - the deploy job runs on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, jobs "are not run in an
    isolated container, even if they use environments", so environment secrets there must be
    treated like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5). Self-hosted runners "can be persistently
    compromised by untrusted code" from anyone who can open a PR, and runner groups limit only which
    repositories use them (📖 R3.5.2); in a monorepo any workflow can likely target the runner's label (⚠️ G15).
    How to restrict a runner to one workflow is not researched (⚠️ G15); just-in-time runners exist
    (📖 R3.5.2, not read in detail). If reaching k0s needs a self-hosted runner, that
    runner is dedicated to the `production` deploy, and the residual risk is recorded;
  - that environment secret is the single source of truth: no copy elsewhere (OD1);
  - an owner, an expiry and rotation in the exception register;
  - optionally a separate environment (e.g. `production-k0s`), limited to `main` and referenced
    only by the k0s/Firebase deploy workflow, so AWS deploy jobs cannot read these secrets
    [design].

  Residual risk: admins can change the environment, and a deleted environment comes back without
  protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); the alerts and settings comparison in layer 7 cover this. The exception
  covers **CI deploy credentials only**. Runtime credentials, such as a k0s autoscaler's AWS access to
  add or remove nodes, live in the cluster, not in GitHub; they follow layer 1 (no static keys, a
  role attached to the machine; ⚠️ not researched for k0s, G1).
- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).
- **Pinning:** workflow lockfile (`gh actions-lock`) or full SHA, enforced by the org policy "Require
  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA" (availability on Team ⚠️); the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so
  the deploy workflow lives in the same repo (📖 R3.5.5; conclusion [design]).
- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,
  `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, `.devcontainer/` (📖 R3.2.8; list ⚠️ R6.5 #5, R6.3.11), plus
  `.npmrc` (registry redirection) [design], the policy packs, the SCP code and the
  catalogue file. This is the canonical L3 path list that layer 3 refers to. Not on it:
  `deploy-approvals/<stack>/`, owned by the stack's owners and the on-call group (OD8, OD9). The private plugin
  marketplace is a separate repo and needs its own ruleset and CODEOWNERS [design]. CI validates the file, because
  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7).
- **No privileged triggers with untrusted code** (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` + checkout,
  📖 R3.5.4).
- **Agent review:** an independent agent (not the one that made the change) may post an automated
  review as an extra check; it never counts as an approval (GĐ-11).
- **Agents in CI:** `claude-code-action` with a custom GitHub App limited to Contents, Issues, Pull
  requests (📖 R1.7.8), whose own credentials are listed in the S2 inventory (⚠️ G19); Anthropic workload identity federation, not a personal OAuth token (📖 R1.7.6);
  `--restricted` and explicit `--tools` (D3; passing it through `claude_args` unverified, ⚠️ research
  6.9.4 Q5); a managed-settings file on the runner, which also guards against mods (📖 R1.5.6; for
  federation auth ⚠️); MCP set fixed by CI because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
  (📖 R1.3.5); never `environment: production` (⚠️ R3.6 #4). Hosted runners give `sudo` (📖 R3.5.1),
  so with `Bash` in `--tools` the runner file is advisory (⚠️ R3.5.1, R3.6 #4).
- **App-opened PRs:** a required check set by a dedicated GitHub App, pinned as its source (layer 3), confirms at least one approval by a
  human who did not trigger the run; counting approvals is not enough, since the app's own approval
  might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3; 📖 R3.2.5).
- **Required checks (S10):** from phase 1, secret scanning, dependency check, SAST (products: G4);
  from phase 2, IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and Pulumi policy packs
  (📖 R4.2.2). For Serverless stacks, Access Analyzer would check the IAM policies in the
  CloudFormation template that `serverless package` produces, against the deployed ones (⚠️ not
  researched); policy packs do not apply to them. Until phase 2, the only compensation for OD8 is
  the risk stop, which fires on every IAM change in the prod preview.

**Audit evidence.** Workflows and lockfile in git; audit-log events such as
`org.update_actions_secret`, `repo.set_workflow_permission_can_approve_pr`, `repository_ruleset.update`
(📖 R3.3.3, R3.5.6). An audit event for environment-secret changes was not researched (⚠️); the
settings comparison in layer 7 covers the S2 exception meanwhile. Check results per PR; secrets inventory (S2).

**Cost / value.** One-time migration to OIDC and pinned actions; slower action updates. Compliance
gets S2 and the same guardrails for agent and human code.

1	"""E3: design conditions on the GitHub Actions workflows that linters do not know about.
     2	
     3	Framework layer 3, "Merge approval = deploy approval", holds only if:
     4	  - only the reusable deploy workflow references `production`;
     5	  - it has no ref/SHA input and is not reachable from workflow_dispatch;
     6	  - no workflow uses `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`;
     7	  - one concurrency group per stack, without cancel-in-progress.
     8	Layer 5 adds: every `uses:` pinned to a full commit SHA (or the same-repository `$/` form),
     9	`permissions:` declared per job with an empty workflow default, and `id-token: write` only
    10	where OIDC is needed.
    11	
    12	Scope: the files in examples/github/workflows only, not a whole monorepo.
    13	"""
    14	import glob
    15	import os
    16	import re
    17	import shlex
    18	import unittest
    19	
    20	import yaml
    21	
    22	HERE = os.path.dirname(__file__)
    23	WF_DIR = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "github", "workflows")
    24	DEPLOY = "deploy-prod.yml"
    25	OIDC_JOBS = {("deploy-prod.yml", "deploy"), ("pr-preview-nonprod.yml", "preview")}
    26	OIDC_CALLERS = {("deploy-on-main.yml", "claims-data"), ("deploy-on-main.yml", "claims-api")}
    27	FORBIDDEN_TRIGGERS = {"issue_comment", "pull_request_target", "workflow_run"}
    28	SHA_PIN = re.compile(r"^[\w.-]+/[\w./-]+@[0-9a-f]{40}$")
    29	SELF_REPO = re.compile(r"^\$/\.github/workflows/[\w.-]+\.ya?ml$")
    30	
    31	
    32	def read(name):
    33	    with open(os.path.join(WF_DIR, name)) as f:
    34	        return f.read()
    35	
    36	
    37	def load_all():
    38	    out = {}
    39	    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(WF_DIR, "*.yml"))):
    40	        with open(path) as f:
    41	            # PyYAML (YAML 1.1) reads the key `on` as True.
    42	            doc = yaml.safe_load(f)
    43	        doc["on"] = doc.pop(True, doc.get("on"))
    44	        out[os.path.basename(path)] = doc
    45	    return out
    46	
    47	
    48	def triggers(doc):
    49	    on = doc["on"]
    50	    if isinstance(on, str):
    51	        return {on}
    52	    if isinstance(on, list):
    53	        return set(on)
    54	    return set(on.keys())
    55	
    56	
    57	def environment_name(job):
    58	    env = job.get("environment")
    59	    if isinstance(env, dict):
    60	        return env.get("name")
    61	    return env
    62	
    63	
    64	class WorkflowPolicyTest(unittest.TestCase):
    65	    @classmethod
    66	    def setUpClass(cls):
    67	        cls.wfs = load_all()
    68	
    69	    def test_files_found(self):
    70	        self.assertIn(DEPLOY, self.wfs)
    71	        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(self.wfs), 3)
    72	
    73	    def test_only_deploy_workflow_uses_production(self):
    74	        for name, doc in self.wfs.items():
    75	            for job_id, job in doc["jobs"].items():
    76	                env = environment_name(job)
    77	                if env and str(env).startswith("production"):
    78	                    self.assertEqual((name, job_id), (DEPLOY, "deploy"))
    79	
    80	    def test_deploy_is_reusable_only(self):
    81	        self.assertEqual(triggers(self.wfs[DEPLOY]), {"workflow_call"})
    82	
    83	    def test_deploy_has_no_ref_or_sha_input(self):
    84	        inputs = self.wfs[DEPLOY]["on"]["workflow_call"].get("inputs", {})
    85	        for key in inputs:
    86	            self.assertNotRegex(key.lower(), r"ref|sha|commit|branch|tag")
    87	
    88	    def test_deploy_checks_out_the_running_commit(self):
    89	        for step in self.wfs[DEPLOY]["jobs"]["deploy"]["steps"]:
    90	            if str(step.get("uses", "")).startswith("actions/checkout@"):
    91	                self.assertNotIn("ref", step.get("with", {}))
    92	                self.assertNotIn("repository", step.get("with", {}))
    93	
    94	    def test_no_forbidden_triggers_and_no_manual_deploy(self):
    95	        for name, doc in self.wfs.items():
    96	            with self.subTest(workflow=name):
    97	                self.assertFalse(triggers(doc) & FORBIDDEN_TRIGGERS)
    98	                calls_deploy = any(
    99	                    str(j.get("uses", "")).endswith("/" + DEPLOY) for j in doc["jobs"].values()
   100	                )
   101	                if calls_deploy:
   102	                    self.assertNotIn("workflow_dispatch", triggers(doc))
   103	                    self.assertEqual(doc["on"]["push"]["branches"], ["main"])
   104	
   105	    def test_deploy_concurrency_per_stack_never_cancelled(self):
   106	        conc = self.wfs[DEPLOY]["jobs"]["deploy"]["concurrency"]
   107	        self.assertIn("inputs.stack", conc["group"])
   108	        self.assertIs(conc["cancel-in-progress"], False)
   109	
   110	    def steps(self):
   111	        return self.wfs[DEPLOY]["jobs"]["deploy"]["steps"]
   112	
   113	    def test_apply_commands_use_only_allowed_flags(self):
   114	        # Tokenised, so short forms (-f = --skip-preview, -t = --target) are caught too.
   115	        allowed = {
   116	            ("pulumi", "up"): {"--stack", "--yes", "--policy-pack"},
   117	            ("pulumi", "preview"): {"--stack", "--json"},
   118	            ("npx", "serverless"): {"--stage", "--package", "--json"},
   119	        }
   120	        seen = set()
   121	        for step in self.steps():
   122	            for line in step.get("run", "").splitlines():
   123	                tokens = shlex.split(line.split(">")[0])
   124	                if len(tokens) < 2:
   125	                    continue
   126	                key = (tokens[0], tokens[1])
   127	                if key in allowed:
   128	                    seen.add(key)
   129	                    flags = {t.split("=")[0] for t in tokens if t.startswith("-")}
   130	                    self.assertLessEqual(flags, allowed[key], line)
   131	        self.assertEqual(seen, set(allowed))
   132	        text = read(DEPLOY)
   133	        for bad in ("pulumi state", "pulumi import", "pulumi destroy", "pulumi refresh", "deploy function"):
   134	            self.assertNotIn(bad, text)
   135	
   136	    def test_risk_stop_cannot_be_skipped_or_ignored(self):
   137	        job = self.wfs[DEPLOY]["jobs"]["deploy"]
   138	        self.assertNotIn("continue-on-error", job)
   139	        [stop] = [s for s in self.steps() if s.get("name") == "Risk stop"]
   140	        self.assertNotIn("continue-on-error", stop)
   141	        self.assertNotIn("if", stop)
   142	        run = " ".join(stop["run"].split())
   143	        self.assertTrue(run.startswith("python3 tools/risk-stop/classify.py "), run)
   144	        for token in ("||", "&&", ";", "|", "&", "$(", "`"):
   145	            self.assertNotIn(token, run)
   146	
   147	    def test_apply_runs_only_after_a_passing_risk_stop(self):
   148	        names = [s.get("name", "") for s in self.steps()]
   149	        stop = names.index("Risk stop")
   150	        applies = [(i, s) for i, s in enumerate(self.steps()) if s.get("name", "").startswith("Apply")]
   151	        self.assertEqual(len(applies), 2)
   152	        for i, s in applies:
   153	            self.assertGreater(i, stop)
   154	            self.assertNotIn("continue-on-error", s)
   155	            self.assertIn(s["if"], ("inputs.tool == 'pulumi'", "inputs.tool == 'serverless'"))
   156	        for s in self.steps()[stop + 1:]:
   157	            self.assertNotIn("continue-on-error", s)
   158	
   159	    def test_dependencies_installed_before_prod_credentials(self):
   160	        creds = next(i for i, s in enumerate(self.steps())
   161	                     if str(s.get("uses", "")).startswith("aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@"))
   162	        npm = next(i for i, s in enumerate(self.steps()) if s.get("run", "").strip() == "npm ci")
   163	        self.assertLess(npm, creds)
   164	
   165	    def test_full_history_for_approval_checks(self):
   166	        [co] = [s for s in self.steps() if str(s.get("uses", "")).startswith("actions/checkout@")]
   167	        self.assertEqual(co["with"].get("fetch-depth"), 0)
   168	
   169	    def test_actions_pinned(self):
   170	        for name, doc in self.wfs.items():
   171	            for job_id, job in doc["jobs"].items():
   172	                if "uses" in job:  # reusable workflow call
   173	                    self.assertRegex(job["uses"], SELF_REPO, f"{name}:{job_id}")
   174	                for step in job.get("steps", []):
   175	                    if "uses" in step:
   176	                        self.assertRegex(step["uses"], SHA_PIN, f"{name}:{job_id}")
   177	
   178	    def test_permissions_per_job(self):
   179	        for name, doc in self.wfs.items():
   180	            with self.subTest(workflow=name):
   181	                self.assertEqual(doc.get("permissions"), {}, "workflow default must be empty")
   182	                for job_id, job in doc["jobs"].items():
   183	                    self.assertIn("permissions", job, f"{name}:{job_id}")
   184	
   185	    def test_id_token_only_where_needed(self):
   186	        for name, doc in self.wfs.items():
   187	            for job_id, job in doc["jobs"].items():
   188	                has = (job.get("permissions") or {}).get("id-token") == "write"
   189	                needed = (name, job_id) in OIDC_JOBS | OIDC_CALLERS
   190	                self.assertEqual(has, needed, f"{name}:{job_id}")
   191	
   192	    def test_no_aws_keys(self):
   193	        for name in self.wfs:
   194	            text = read(name)
   195	            self.assertNotRegex(text, r"aws-access-key-id|aws-secret-access-key|AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY")

1	"""E2: CODEOWNERS gives each path the owners the framework requires.
     2	
     3	Resolves the *effective* owners of sample paths with GitHub's rule "the last matching
     4	pattern takes the most precedence" (GitHub docs, about-code-owners), so a broad line
     5	placed after the L3 section would make this test fail.
     6	
     7	The pattern matcher implements the gitignore subset CODEOWNERS supports: leading `/`
     8	anchors to the root, trailing `/` matches a directory and everything below it, `*`
     9	does not cross `/`, `**` does, and a pattern with no inner `/` matches at any depth.
    10	It is checked against the examples in GitHub's docs (MatcherTest). It is a model of
    11	GitHub's behaviour, not GitHub itself.
    12	
    13	Not checked (needs the real repository): that teams exist and have write access.
    14	GitHub skips such owners silently.
    15	"""
    16	import os
    17	import re
    18	import unittest
    19	
    20	import yaml
    21	
    22	HERE = os.path.dirname(__file__)
    23	CODEOWNERS = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "github", "CODEOWNERS")
    24	
    25	L3 = "@example-org/l3-owners"
    26	ONCALL = "@example-org/oncall-approvers"
    27	
    28	# Canonical L3 path list, framework layer 5 "CODEOWNERS" bullet, one sample file each.
    29	PROCESS_L3_SAMPLES = [
    30	    ".github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml",
    31	    ".github/CODEOWNERS",
    32	    "CLAUDE.md",
    33	    "services/claims/CLAUDE.md",        # nested CLAUDE.md inside a domain path
    34	    "CLAUDE.local.md",
    35	    ".claude/settings.json",
    36	    "services/claims/.claude/settings.json",
    37	    ".claude.json",
    38	    ".mcp.json",
    39	    "services/claims/.mcp.json",
    40	    ".husky/pre-commit",
    41	    ".gitmodules",
    42	    ".ripgreprc",
    43	    ".devcontainer/devcontainer.json",
    44	    ".npmrc",
    45	    "services/claims/.npmrc",
    46	    "policy-packs/aws/index.ts",
    47	    "tools/risk-stop/classify.py",     # [design] not yet in the framework's layer-5 list
    48	    "infra/pulumi/org-scp/index.ts",
    49	    "agent-config/managed-settings.json",
    50	]
    51	
    52	# Deployable paths: (sample file, domain team that must be an owner).
    53	DEPLOYABLE_SAMPLES = [
    54	    ("services/claims/serverless.yml", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    55	    ("services/claims/src/handler.ts", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    56	    ("services/underwriting/serverless.yml", "@example-org/team-underwriting"),
    57	    ("web/firebase.json", "@example-org/team-web"),
    58	    ("infra/pulumi/claims-data/index.ts", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    59	    ("k8s/claims/deployment.yaml", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    60	    ("infra/pulumi/iam/index.ts", L3),
    61	]
    62	
    63	RISK_STOP_SAMPLES = [
    64	    ("deploy-approvals/claims-data/0123abcd.yaml", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    65	    ("deploy-approvals/iam/0123abcd.yaml", L3),
    66	]
    67	
    68	
    69	def pattern_to_regex(pattern):

# ADR-0004: Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until a stack owner approves the prod preview

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (OD8, OD11, OD13)
- **Scope:** deploy workflows for Pulumi and Serverless stacks; k0s and Firebase not covered yet

## 1. Context

With the gate at merge time (ADR-0003), the approver reviews the code change, not the prod diff. A
PR may not preview prod, because that would run PR code with state-write and secret access
(📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). So a stateful delete or an IAM change can reach prod without anyone
seeing its real effect. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files such as
`serverless.yml`, not in separate L3 paths (assumed ⚠️; we have no access to the repo).

## 2. Options considered

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. Accept the gap | No extra step | Destructive diffs applied unseen |
| B. Risk stop, approved by the L3 owner team | Specialist review | Often a third person; L3 team must be on call 24/7 |
| C. Risk stop, approved by an owner of the stack | Stays at two people; works at night | Less specialist review; compensated by automated checks |

## 3. Decision

Option C [design]. The deploy job on `main` previews prod. On stateful replace/delete, an IAM
change, a network or security-group change, or (from phase 2) an advisory policy finding, it stops
and posts the filtered preview. The original author opens a PR (the workflow does not, as "Allow GitHub Actions to create and
approve pull requests" stays off, 📖 R3.3.3; ⚠️ R3.6 #3) adding
`deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` with the SHA and preview hash (owned by the stack's owners and the
on-call group, OD8, OD9); the first approver approves it
(OD13). If that approver is unavailable, another stack owner approves; this makes three people and
is recorded as a deviation (OD11). After the merge the workflow previews again on the new HEAD and
continues only if the hash matches. Serverless uses `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI because
differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2). A `mandatory` Pulumi policy violation always
blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2; policy packs from phase 2).

## 4. Consequences

- **Positive:** the person who approves now sees the prod diff for the changes that can do lasting
  damage. Still two people in the normal case.
- **Negative / trade-offs:** while a stack is stopped, later deploys to it stop too (the hash
  differs), including an incident fix, until the approval lands or the change is reverted. One more review round when the stop fires.
- **Risks & how we watch them:** preview output may not be stable enough to hash (⚠️ Options §8); if

Independent review: the `examples/` step-1 artifacts (round 2)

`validate.sh` passes as claimed (✅ I ran it with the given actionlint and zizmor: 54 tests OK, zizmor "No findings", actionlint and yamllint clean). The workflow, ruleset, environment and CODEOWNERS fixes from round 1 hold. The two GitHub-docs claims also hold (📖 I fetched the github/docs source): the `$/.github/workflows/...` syntax is recommended there, and a pending run is cancelled and replaced by a newer one. The approval binding in the risk stop is still bypassable, though, and three bypasses reproduce. The scripts and throwaway repos are in `/tmp/claude-1001/-home-do-hoang-minh-hung-papaya-devsecops-challenge/6db3dd9e-1a2b-4563-ab89-a7de7a1f8366/scratchpad/review2/exp.py`.

HIGH

H1. **The approval check reads the file's current contents but only checks the commit that first added it.**
- Where: `risk-stop/classify.py:179` and `classify.py:188-196`.
- Problem: `--diff-filter=A` finds the commit that added the file. Later edits to the file are never checked, and the values are read from the working tree. So one PR can change an existing, legitimately added approval file (new `preview_hash`) together with a new risky IAM change. This works with squash merges too.
- Evidence: experiment A returned exit 0 (deploy continues).
- Impact: this breaks the README claim (Finding 2; E7 row) that "a PR cannot carry its own risky change and its approval". As a side effect, a Pulumi program or Serverless plugin can also rewrite the file at runtime, before the classifier reads it.
- Fix:
  - Read the fields with `git show <added>:<rel>`.
  - Reject the file if `git log --format=%H -- <rel>` lists more than one commit, or require the file at HEAD to be byte-identical to the added version.
  - Add a test for this case.

H2. **Merge commits let one PR carry both the risky change and its own approval.**
- Where: `github/ruleset-main.json:15-24` and `classify.py:186-196`.
- Problem: the PR has commit C1 (risky change), then commit C2 (only `deploy-approvals/<stack>/C1.yaml`, with the predicted hash), and is merged with a merge commit. C1 is a strict ancestor of HEAD, and C2 touches only the approvals folder. The binding only works if every PR lands as one squashed commit, but nothing enforces squash.
- Evidence: experiment B returned exit 0.
- Fix:
  - Add `"allowed_merge_methods": ["squash"]` to the `pull_request` rule. The extracted schema has the key (`schemas/github-ruleset-create.json:297`).
  - In the classifier, require both `stopped_commit` and the adding commit to be on `git rev-list --first-parent HEAD`.
  - Add a test.
  - State the squash-only dependency in the README and as a [design] finding.
- Side benefit: today, with merge commits, the 7-day age check uses a committer date that the PR author controls. Squash-only fixes that too.

H3. **Re-running an old deploy run puts an older commit into prod without any approval.**
- Where: `github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml` (no check for a current HEAD), and it is not covered in the framework's layer 3 conditions.
- Evidence (📖 [Re-running workflows and jobs](https://github.com/github/docs/blob/main/content/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs.md)):
  - "People with write permissions to a repository can re-run workflows".
  - Runs can be re-run "up to 30 days after its initial run".
  - A re-run uses "the same `GITHUB_SHA` … and `GITHUB_REF`".
  - So `production`'s main-only branch rule still passes.
- Impact: any writer, or their agent with a write token, can re-run the deploy of an older commit and roll prod back. Nobody approved that change. The risk stop catches only risky reverse diffs, not code or config rollbacks.
- None of the repo's docs, ADRs or examples mention re-runs; I searched for "re-run" and found nothing.
- Fix: as the first step after checkout, fail unless `github.sha` equals `git rev-parse origin/main` (available because of `fetch-depth: 0`). Also add it to the layer-3 condition list and to the tests.

MEDIUM

M1. **An approval can be merged before the risky change it covers.**
- Where: `classify.py:186-192`.
- Problem: nothing checks that `stopped_commit` was actually stopped, or that the approved code is the code at HEAD.
- Example: PR Y adds an approval with `stopped_commit` set to the current main tip and a predicted hash, and merges first. Then PR X merges the risky change. The deploy continues. The hash is predictable for a create, since old inputs are `{}`.
- Evidence: experiment C returned exit 0.
- Impact: the approver of Y signs a hash without any stop summary. So the README claim "only with the git history the framework's flow produces" (E7 row, `tests/test_risk_stop.py:4-5`) is overstated.
- Fix (either):
  - require `git diff --quiet <stopped_commit> HEAD -- <workdir>`, passing `--workdir` to the classifier; or
  - check through the API that the run for `stopped_commit` failed at the "Risk stop" step.
- Either way, mark it [design] and list it for the owner.

M2. **The "safety net" for types missing from the lists does not apply to creates.**
- Where: `classify.py:136-138`, which applies the property-name rule only to `update`/`replace`. Also the regex at `classify.py:111-115`.
- Evidence: I ran each case through `reasons_for`; every one returned `[]`, i.e. not risky:
  - `aws:ecr/repositoryPolicy` create with `policy`;
  - `aws:s3/bucketAclV2` create with `acl`;
  - `aws-native:iam:Role` create (a different provider prefix);
  - `publiclyAccessible` / `PubliclyAccessible` update on RDS (the regex has `publicaccess`, which does not match);
  - `aws:cloudtrail/trail` update of `enableLogging` (an audit trail switched off).
- Why it matters: the README Limits section calls the property-name rule "the safety net for missing types", and framework layer 3 says every IAM or network change stops.
- Fix:
  - On create, apply the key rule to the keys present.
  - Add `public`, `aws-native:` equivalents, and a `cloudtrail`/logging-disable rule.
  - Or soften the README claim, and accept more stops (every new Lambda with a `role` would then stop).

M3. **Some prod-credentialed code is fetched or installed after the credentials step, so the "dependencies before credentials" claim is only partly true.**
- Where: `deploy-prod.yml:67-131`; `test_workflow_policy.py:159-163` only checks `npm ci`.
- Two cases (⚠️ both from memory, not verified here):
  - Serverless v4: the `serverless` npm package downloads the sf-core framework at first run. That happens inside `npx serverless package` / `diff`, after the credentials step.
  - Pulumi: provider plugins are downloaded during `preview`, and `--policy-pack policy-packs/aws` needs its own `node_modules`, which nothing installs.
- Also: the policy pack is referenced in phase 1 although the comment says "phase 2". If the directory does not exist, every `pulumi up` fails.
- Fix:
  - Verify both behaviours.
  - Pre-install sf-core, the plugins (`pulumi plugin install` or `pulumi install`) and the policy-pack dependencies before the AWS credentials step.
  - Or guard the policy-pack flag until phase 2.
  - Narrow the README wording.

LOW
- L1 `test_workflow_policy.py:147-157`: only steps whose name starts with "Apply" have their `if:` checked. A step named something else, with `if: failure()` and `run: pulumi up --stack x --yes`, would pass all tests. The flag test also misses `npx sls …` and `env X=… pulumi up …`. Fix: check the `if:` of any step after the stop whose run contains `pulumi up` or `serverless deploy`, and forbid `failure()`, `always()` and `cancelled()` there.
- L2 `classify.py:208-214`: the file name is not checked against `stopped_commit`, and the `stack:` field is not checked against the directory name. The framework says the file name is `<sha>`.
- L3: a valid approval for hash H stays reusable for 7 days. Experiment F: revert, then re-apply the same IAM change, and the deploy continues without a new approval. If this is intended, state it.
- L4 `adapters.py:76-84`: the comment says `Code` is left out of the hash "not out of the risk check", but it is popped from `changed_keys` too. Also (⚠️) `AWS::Lambda::Alias` and provisioned concurrency refer to the version logical ID, which changes on every build, so the hash may never be stable for such services.
- L5 `adapters.py:49`: the URN fallback takes the type from `urn.split("::")[-2]`. For child resources that part is `parent$type`, so the prefix matching fails. Use the part after the last `$`.
- L6 `github/environment-production/secrets.md:9` links to `examples/aws/oidc-trust-prod-deploy.json`, which does not exist yet (E4 is planned). Mark it as planned.
- L7: the repo paths differ between the examples and the workflow, and the README does not say how they map. The examples use `examples/risk-stop/` and `risk-stop/deploy-approvals/…`. The workflow and CODEOWNERS use `tools/risk-stop/` and `deploy-approvals/`. The plan's E7 row names `adapters/pulumi.py` and `adapters/serverless.py`, but there is one `adapters.py`. State the mapping in the README.
- L8 README E2 row: "domain team **and** on-call group" can read as two approvals being required. Under GitHub's code-owner rule one approval from either team is enough, as the framework says (📖 R3.2.7). Reword it to "co-owned by".
- L9 [design] items not listed in "Findings from writing these files": the property-name rule and the rule that an unknown operation stops the deploy both go beyond the framework's categories. Add them to the findings for the owner.

Rule compliance: no real account IDs, ARNs, emails or names in `examples/` (✅ grep). Placeholders are used throughout. Nothing touched live infrastructure. The ✅/📖/⚠️ markers are mostly correct. The overstated claims are the risk-stop ones in H1, H2 and M1 (README E7 row and Finding 2, `tests/test_risk_stop.py:4-5`), plus the "safety net" and "before prod credentials" wording in M2 and M3.

Verdict: not ready. Three HIGH findings remain: the approval file is not bound to the commit that added it, merges are not squash-only, and an old deploy run can be re-run. The rest of E1, E2, E3 and E3b holds; fix these three and soften the E7 claims, then re-review.
